Row.Text: Toyotomi Hideyoshi sits across the go table from the monk, a legendary master. One by one, click by clack, the stones fall across the board. When the game is done, Toyotomi is defeated. Again.
Focus on mass construction – the perception of strength is strength.

What is significant about the construction of a wonder? It is not the artistry, the skill of the craftspeople, the aesthetic of the final form. No – it is the determined effort, the organization and sense of purpose that led to this. The same dedication that led masons to lay bricks with regular precision could lead archers to aim and soldiers to strike.
Found a Settlement within 5 tiles of another Player's Settlement's City-Center.
Focus on aggression – boldness is strength.
A messenger unfurls the battle map atop Toyotomi’s go board. Toyotomi surveys his troop positions, and the enemy defenses. “Atari,” he mutters, pleased.
Toyotomi takes his sword and neatly slices the board in two. Game over.

The theater performance begins. A crash and laughter as Hyottoko puts his foot in a pail and falls face-first. A blur of motion and color as jugglers obscure the scene. A blare of festive music. The audience is enthralled. Toyotomi is not. It is all rather shallow.
Seek out something with more substance.
A new art form, Noh, takes shape, under Toyotomi’s patronage. It embraces the weird, the strange, the otherworldly – the sublime.
Have a Wonder in 3 different Settlements.
But the masses seem to like it.

Toyotomi sits in the military camp, watching soldiers come and go, without saying a word. He raises a finger to silence any questions, and goes back to watching. People – even soldiers at war – do not see the world as it is. Rather, they see things as they expect to see them. As such, they are predictable.
Victory, then, comes from breaking the pattern.
Soldiers unprepared are not soldiers; they are men. And then they are corpses.
Defeat 3 Units in a single Turn.
Search the ancient archives for insights.

Slow percussion. Strangely drawn-out sung dialogue. Masks. The Noh theater is in session. Toyotomi sits rapt, transported by its otherworldly aesthetic. Next to him, a high-ranking minister snores softly.
Perhaps the commoners would like something more… common.
More! Fund the theaters! Write new performances!

Diplomats for Toyotomi have great hopes for his alliance with Friedrich the Great – each man is a military master, and each professes a great love for theater. But, too, there is difference: the refined and nobly-born Friedrich, and the self-made warrior Hideyoshi. The court waits as Hideyoshi’s eyes scan Friedrich’s latest letter.
“Baka!” Hideyoshi exclaims as he tosses the letter aside.
When you start an Endeavor with Friedrich, Oblique, +5 Relationship.
“Omoshiroi!” Hideyoshi smiles as he carefully folds the letter.
When you start a Sanction with Friedrich, Oblique, -5 Relationship.

Toyotomi watches his soldiers spar. Each moves with the other, a blend of apprehension, waiting, evaluation, and movement. They are, he thinks, dancing more than fighting.
The War of Drama, the Drama of War

To conquer, one needs to do more than seize strategic fortresses or establish lines of control. Ways of thought, of imagination, of dreaming can also be conquered. Toyotomi muses on how to wage war with minds as well as bodies.
The War of Drama, the Drama of War
The first step is to remove the enemy’s resources.
A people, lacking a cultural output, may better welcome foreign rule.
Pillage a Kiln, Pavilion, Unique Building, or Unique Improvement.
The first step is to improve our own imaginations.
Securing supplies for the theater is constantly a struggle in wartime. Nonethless, Toyotomi’s theater is always the best arrayed. The important things matter.
Fire flickers on stone lamps; its reflection shimmers on dancers’ costumes. Watching the theater, Toyotomi thinks on cities he has seen burning.
Improve 3 more Resources in Distant Lands.

Toyotomi reviews his troops – too few, especially considering the threat that lies beyond his borders. But the opportune time may not wait for him to be prepared. Perhaps strategy and sheer boldness will overcome numbers.
Toyotomi’s overseas adventures have been successful. His ships cross the ocean and – for the most part – reach their destinations. This time.
Army Commander with Infantry, Ranged, Cavalry, and Siege Unit.
Each conquest is a mirror of the glory of Toyotomi’s capital. A dim mirror, but with the shadow of an image of beauty.
Build a Wonder in a Settlement Captured this Age in Distant Lands.

{1_CIVILIZATION_ADJ} society is an armed society. Carrying a weapon is a marker of status, especially for veterans. When tempers flare, swords are unsheathed, and disagreements become murders. Or, Hideyoshi thinks, they may become revolutions.
Let them keep the swords. An armed society needs less training.

The katanagari begins: the sword-hunt. Farmers’ houses are ransacked, granaries searched, and piles upon piles of blades accumulate. Thus far, the noble families have been successful in bribing, pleading, or challenging their way out of the hunt, but they, especially, might pose a threat to Hideyoshi.
Nobles can bear swords. Commoners cannot. That is the edict.
The nobles had better sharpen their tongues instead. Grab their swords.

Toyotomi looks over the foreign missionaries, his gaze flickering from one face to the other. They claim a mission of peace and love and say that they follow no authority but the divine. But words of peace can hide daggers as well as the sleeve of a kamishimo. What master do they really serve?
They are who they say they are.
They seek to undermine Toyotomi’s rule.

The missionaries have been sent to confer with their purported master – in heaven. This will cause a diplomatic incident. But within the palace, Toyotomi Hideyoshi sleeps securely. But his diplomats wonder what to tell the foreign powers.

Toyotomi’s ambition has cost him – outside of his lands, he is thought of as best as a ruthless opportunist, at worst, a tyrant. But these are stories, and like stories, they can be written, revised, and acted anew. Toyotomi sets brush to paper – he will author the story of his own life. He writes…
His struggles as Hiyoshimaru, the peasant.
His conquests in battle, as kanpaku.
More deadly than arbalests and arquebuses is fear. As the clash of weapons rises, the enemy collapses – Hideyoshi’s boldness has become in itself a weapon.
Like an avalanche, fear builds upon fear.
“If you do not sing, I will convince you.” So goes the popular anecdote about Toyotomi’s rule – with persuasion or coercion, he will get his way. But there are still those who are not convinced.
Make an example – all will sing for Toyotomi.
The actors sing. They smile. They dance. Soldiers march in the street.
Build 3 Wonders in Settlements Captured this Age.
Toyotomi has never fled from the possibilities of a new age. Now, the world is broken and made anew each passing year. He has learned to conquer the land and sea – he casts his gaze skyward.
The sword is intimate. But bombs are more effective.

As Toyotomi’s bombers lift off from the airfield, he realizes: this is the new face of war. He grips the radio receiver as his fingers ache for the katana. He speaks commands to level cities into a telephone; his throat wants to shout orders across the battlefield.

The Noh actor wears a mask like the soldier wears a helmet: each seeks to overpower, each seeks to impose their own reality upon a resistant world. Toyotomi is as at home in the theater as he is on the battlefield. Theaters in cities Toyotomi has conquered compete to honor his legacy.
They will show the richness gained in conquest.
+1 Resource Slot in Settlements with an Opera House and which were Captured this Age.
They will be places where foreign ways are better understood.

Like the moon, Japan waxes and wanes, but remains a constant force: the inward pull of Heian, the chaotic frenzy of Sengoku, and now the Meiji rush towards the future. Over all of it, Hideyoshi’s vision. His quest…
Himiko and Hideyoshi Go to Himeji

The courtyard of Himeji castle hosts a matsuri each new year: colorful umbrellas splashing the white castle walls with yellows, reds, greens and blues. In the center are carts full of food: onigiri stuffed with radish, steaming bowls of fried-tofu soba, dango dumplings roasting on skewers. This year, Toyotomi has brought his ally, Himiko.
Let Himiko take charge of the matsuri food vendors.
Let Himiko take charge of the matsuri amusements.
